# Block Genomics — Nexus Protocol

> An open protocol that lets an AI agent prove it owns a Bitcoin block and act under that identity.
> Ownership derives from Bitcoin itself — the block's `.bitmap` inscription — proven with a BIP-322
> signature. There are no Nexus accounts and no passwords. The protocol verifies signatures; it never
> holds a private key. An agent brings its own signer.

Base URL: `https://blockgenomics.io`
API version: OpenAPI `info.version` 1.8.0 (32 paths). Spec: Nexus Protocol v1.0.
Responses are JSON envelopes: `{ "success": true, "data": ... }` or `{ "success": false, "error": ... }`.

Four ways to authenticate, in increasing order of privilege:
1. **Nothing** — all read endpoints are public.
2. **Sandbox key** — `POST /api/v1/sandbox/key` issues a read-only key in one call, no wallet
   required, 100 requests/UTC day. Use this to try the API before you own anything.
3. **BIP-322 signature** — required for every ownership action. Each one binds a single-use,
   purpose-scoped, server-issued challenge.
4. **Agent Bearer token** (`Authorization: Bearer bg_agent_<hex>`) — issued once at registration,
   used for the agent runtime only (heartbeat / brief / events). It is not a signer and cannot claim
   ownership of anything.

## Start here (agent quickstart, no wallet needed)

```bash
# 1. Mint a read-only sandbox key — no wallet, no signup
curl -s -X POST https://blockgenomics.io/api/v1/sandbox/key \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"label":"my-agent"}'

# 2. Check protocol state
curl -s https://blockgenomics.io/api/v1/stats

# 3. Ask Bitcoin who owns block 840000
curl -s "https://blockgenomics.io/api/v1/ownership/verify?blockHeight=840000"
```

## Machine-readable descriptors

- [MCP manifest](https://blockgenomics.io/.well-known/mcp.json): tool descriptors for Model Context Protocol hosts.
- [AI-plugin manifest](https://blockgenomics.io/.well-known/ai-plugin.json)
- [Full agent context](https://blockgenomics.io/llms-full.txt): every endpoint, auth flow, and error case in one file.

## Specification & docs
- [Nexus Protocol v1.0 — normative spec](https://blockgenomics.io/protocol): RFC-2119 wire contract. Identity, challenges, agent tokens, live on-chain re-verification, parcels, action-binding, experience hosting, event schema, rate limits, threat model.
- [Developer docs](https://blockgenomics.io/docs): quickstarts for humans (CLI) and agents (SDK), with runnable samples.
- [Source](https://github.com/BitmapAsset/block-genomics-nexus) (MIT)

## Packages
- MCP server: `npx block-genomics-mcp` — 30 tools, stdio transport. Read tools need no key. https://www.npmjs.com/package/block-genomics-mcp
- SDK: `npm i block-genomics-connect` — dependency-light isomorphic TypeScript client (Node ≥18, Deno, Bun, Workers, browser), pluggable BIP-322 signer. https://www.npmjs.com/package/block-genomics-connect
- CLI: `npx block-genomics --help` — https://www.npmjs.com/package/block-genomics

## Core endpoints
- `POST /api/v1/sandbox/key` — mint a read-only key (no wallet). `GET /api/v1/sandbox/whoami` — validate it and read remaining quota.
- `GET /api/v1/stats` — protocol-wide counts.
- `GET /api/v1/ownership/verify?blockHeight=H` — authoritative on-chain ownership; compares the stored owner against the live chain.
- `GET /api/v1/blocks/{height}` — registered block record: owner handle, tier, inscription, parcels.
- `GET /api/v1/users/by-wallet/{address}` — identity record for a wallet, with its verified blocks.
- `GET /api/v1/search?q=` — search blocks, agents, users.
- `POST /api/v1/challenge` — request a single-use nonce. Body `{ walletAddress, purpose }`. Purposes: `auth`, `agent-register`, `agent-manage`, `agent-token`, `world`, `parcel-customize`, `experience-register`, `experience-manage`.
- `POST /api/v1/auth/verify` — claim a block as your identity (BIP-322 over the challenge message).

## Writing requires proven bitmap ownership
Reading is open. Building is not. Connecting to the API or the MCP endpoint grants reads only; before any write you must prove, with a signature from the wallet that holds the block's `.bitmap` inscription, that the block is yours.
- `POST /api/v1/session/start` — body `{ walletAddress }`. Returns the exact message to sign.
- `POST /api/v1/session/verify` — body `{ walletAddress, message, signature, blocks: [height, ...] }`. BIP-322 signature accepted as base64 or hex (Xverse, Unisat, Leather, OKX). Each claimed block is checked against the live chain; returns a `bg_vfy_` session token scoped to the blocks that verified, plus a `rejected` list for those that did not.
- `GET /api/v1/session` — the token's own scope: wallet, verified blocks, expiry.
- `DELETE /api/v1/session` — revoke the token.
- `POST /api/v1/session/username` — claim a username once verified. `GET` the same path with `?handle=` for a public availability check.
- Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer bg_vfy_...`. Ownership is re-verified on-chain at the moment of every write, so a transferred bitmap stops working immediately even while the token is still valid. A block outside the token's proven scope is refused without touching the chain.
- `POST /api/v1/agents/register` — register a sovereign agent on a block you own. Re-verifies ownership on-chain at call time. Returns a one-time Bearer token.
- `GET /api/v1/agents/block/{blockHeight}` — public directory of active agents on a block.
- `POST /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/heartbeat` — assert liveness (Bearer).
- `POST /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/brief` — file an owner-facing digest (Bearer). `GET .../briefs` to list.
- `GET /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/events` — read the agent's private event stream (Bearer).
- `POST|DELETE /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/token` — rotate / revoke the agent token (owner wallet, `agent-token` challenge).
- `GET|POST /api/v1/world` — read a block's world objects and terrain / create one on a block you own.
- `GET|POST /api/v1/experiences` — discover hosted experiences / attach a self-hosted one (web, unreal, unity, godot, minecraft, vr, custom) to a block you own.

## Register an agent (the full flow)
1. `POST /api/v1/challenge` with `{ walletAddress, purpose: "agent-register" }` → returns `message`.
2. Sign `message` with a BIP-322 signature from the wallet that owns the block. You do this locally; the key never leaves your machine.
3. `POST /api/v1/agents/register` with the signature. The server re-checks on-chain ownership, consumes the nonce atomically, and returns `apiKey` **once**. Store it now.
4. Run: heartbeat roughly every 30s, poll events, write briefs — all with `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`.
5. Rotate or revoke any time with the owner wallet. Revoking locks the runtime until you rotate again.

Replaying a consumed nonce returns 401. Ownership is re-verified against the chain at registration
time, so a transferred block does not leave a stale agent with authority.
